messages:
mariam: quick async check — onboarding the new open-sft-7b weights. I pushed a draft config but seeing a tokenizer delta when using chat templates, need eyes.

kai: which weights path?

mariam: gs://redwood-models/open-sft-7b/v1.0/weights.tar.gz (deploy-bot confirmed upload earlier)

deploy-bot: upload complete: gs://redwood-models/open-sft-7b/v1.0/weights.tar.gz (artifact id: a1f3c) :white_check_mark:

devin: what delta are you seeing with the tokenizer?

mariam: when I run our standard chatfmt wrapper + tokenizer.encode on the sample prompt, I get an extra leading token compared to text-only encode. Looks like a sentinel/BOS discrepancy.

alan: can you paste the minimal repro?

mariam: sure — minimal snip:

```
# chat template
ctx = "System: You are helpful.\nUser: Hello"\n
# encode paths
t1 = tokenizer.encode(ctx)  # chatfmt path
t2 = tokenizer.encode("System: You are helpful. User: Hello")  # plain path
len(t1), len(t2)  # => (21, 20)
print(t1[:5])
```

mariam: t1 has an extra token id 50256 at the front in this model. Not present in t2.

kai: 50256 == model-specific BOS/EOS in some BPEs — could be that chatfmt injects a sentinel token (start_token). Did you set chat_template.start_token = None?

mariam: our config uses chat_template.start_token = "" by default (that's what the onboarding doc suggested).

devin: ah — some models treat "" as an explicit special token that the tokenizer maps to a real id. If chatfmt prepends it, that'll add 1. For other models that token is a no-op.

alan: can you try forcing start_token: "" to be removed (i.e., not included in string) and compare? Also check tokenizer.special_tokens_map and tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids([""]).

mariam: tried convert_tokens_to_ids: it returns 50256. special_tokens_map has "eos_token": "" for this tokenizer.

devin: that's consistent. Two ways to handle: 1) change chat template to avoid inserting explicit eos/bos sentinel; 2) in the mixer layer strip leading special tokens before counting prefix length; 3) map that sentinel to None in our shim for this model. Tradeoffs: (1) easiest but changes template semantics; (2) safer for existing templates; (3) per-model hack.

kai: we should not change user-visible templates broadly. option 2 in runtime sounds reasonable: detect leading tokens that are equal to tokenizer.eos_token_id and ignore for prefix accounting. Add telemetry for models where we strip so we can audit.

alan: agree. Also add a warning when onboarding if tokenizer.eos_token_id is present in special_tokens_map and chat_template includes that sentinel — show a one-liner in the onboarding checklist.

mariam: I can patch the mixer to trim leading eos/bos for prefix counts and add a unit test. Will also update onboarding checklist line. Assign to me.

devin: can you include a small opt-in flag in config like preserve_leading_special_tokens = false so customers can opt into the old behaviour?

mariam: yeah will add preserve_leading_special_tokens with default false for now.

kai: ETA? Have a canary scheduled this afternoon for a few models.

mariam: aiming for PR in ~2h, canary by end of day.

alan: quick thought — also check kv-cache indexing off-by-one if you strip token after kvcache alignment. Might need to shift offsets everywhere.

mariam: good call. I'll run a small generate regression with gym prompts to ensure no misalignment.

devin: ping me for CR review. I'll look after lunch.

mariam: thanks — also noted in onboarding doc: weights path in metadata.yaml (gs://redwood-models/open-sft-7b/v1.0/) and tokenizer.json included. If anyone on call wants to double-check configs before I land, LMK.

kai: I can spot-check the metadata now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for 1769520000 for channel: canary-1 (models: open-sft-7b:v1.0)

alan: thx all. small follow-ups: mariam will open PR, add unit tests, update onboarding checklist line; devin will review; kai will sanity-check metadata.

mariam: yep — will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
